title.en: Joseph's Dreams and the Coat of Many Colours

region.en: Valley of Hebron, land of Canaan

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Israel loves the son of his old age more than all his children and makes him a long-sleeved coat. Joseph's sheaves-dream and stars-dream — 'I have dreamed a dream more; behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars bowed down to me' — make even Jacob rebuke him, 'while his father observed the saying.'
summary.zh: 以色列愛年老所生之子過於眾子，為他作長袖彩衣。約瑟的捆禾之夢與星辰之夢——「我又做了一夢，夢見太陽月亮與十一個星向我下拜」——連雅各也責備他，「卻把這話存在心裡」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it his brethren, and said: 'Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and, behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me.' And he told it to his father, and to his brethren; and his father rebuked him, and said unto him: 'What is this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth?'

title.en: Doth Not the Coat Bear Witness? Joseph Sold from the Pit
title.zh: 彩衣為證：約瑟被賣離坑

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Jacob sends Joseph to find his brothers past Shechem to Dothan; they see him from afar — 'behold, this dreamer cometh' — and conspire to kill him. Reuben stays their hands by casting him into a pit; while Reuben is away, Judah's plan sells him to Midianite-Ishmaelite caravan traders for twenty pieces of silver. The brothers dip the coat in goat blood; Jacob rends his clothes and refuses comfort.
summary.zh: 雅各遣約瑟尋兄，經示劍至多坍；眾兄遠見——「那作夢的來了」——謀殺之。流便攔阻，投之於坑；流便離去，猶大之計以二十塊銀子賣之予米甸以實瑪利商隊。眾兄以羊血染彩衣；雅各撕裂衣服，不肯受安慰。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And they said one to another: 'Behold, this dreamer cometh. Come now therefore, and let us slay him, and cast him into some pit; and we will say: An evil beast hath devoured him; and we shall see what will become of his dreams.' And Reuben heard it, and delivered him out of their hand, and said: 'Let us not take his life.'

Reuben planned to return and rescue him, but found the pit empty. Judah proposed profit over murder: 'What profit is it if we slay our brother? Come, and let us sell him'. They drew Joseph up and sold him for twenty pieces of silver to merchantmen bound for Egypt, then slaughtered a kid of the goats and dipped the coat in its blood, sending it to their father with the question, 'This have we found: know now whether it be thy son's coat or no.' Jacob rent his clothes and mourned: 'I will go down into the grave unto my son mourning' — 'and all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted.' Paraphrase of Genesis 37:26-35 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Judah and Tamar: The Firstborn Debt

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Judah's first two sons die after wronging Tamar; he withholds his third from her. Tamar disguises herself as a veiled cult prostitute at the road to Timnah, conceives by Judah, and is about to be burned for harlotry until she produces his seal, cord, and staff: 'Discern, I pray thee, whose these be.' Judah answers: 'She is more righteous than I' — and Perez, ancestor of David, is born.
summary.zh: 猶大長次二子因得罪他瑪而死；他扣下三子不予她。他瑪喬裝蒙面廟妓於往亭拿路口，與猶大同寢有孕；被判為妓當焚，乃出示猶大之印、帶子與杖：「請認一認，這是誰的？」猶大答：「她比我更有義」——其後法勒斯生，為大衛之祖。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Levirate custom (yibbum) etiology; Judah's royal line runs through Tamar's Perez.

passages.text: And it came to pass about three months after, that it was told Judah, saying: 'Tamar thy daughter-in-law hath played the harlot; and also, behold, she is with child by whoredom.' And Judah said: 'Bring her forth, and let her be burnt.'

When she was brought forth she sent to her father-in-law the pledges taken in her disguise: 'By the man, whose these are, I am with child; discern, I pray thee, whose these be'. Judah recognized them and confessed; Tamar bore twins, and at the birth Zerah put out a hand first with a scarlet thread, but Perez pushed through before him — the name Perez meaning 'breach', the line through which David and the kings of Judah descend. Paraphrase of Genesis 38:25-30 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

region.en: Potiphar's house, Egypt (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 波提乏家中，埃及（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The LORD is with Joseph in Potiphar's house, where he rises to overseer of all. His master's wife seizes his garment day after day; he refuses and flees, leaving it in her hand — evidence enough for the lie. Joseph is cast into the king's prison, where 'the keeper of the prison looked not to any thing that was under his hand, because the LORD was with him.'
summary.zh: 耶和華與約瑟同在波提乏家中，升至總管。主母日日扯其衣；他拒絕而逃，衣留其手——足為偽證。約瑟被囚於王囚，而「司獄不查他手下的事，因為耶和華與他同在」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And she caught him by his garment, saying: 'Lie with me'; and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out. And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand, and was fled forth, that she called unto the men of her house.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 39:12-14 (public domain), lightly condensed.

passages.text: She showed the household the 'Hebrew' her husband had brought 'to mock us', producing the garment; Potiphar put Joseph into the prison where the king's prisoners were bound. Even there God was with him, giving him favour with the keeper, who committed all the prisoners to his care — 'because the LORD was with him; and that which he did, the LORD made it to prosper.' Paraphrase of Genesis 39:14-23 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Cupbearer and the Baker Dream in Prison

region.en: King's prison, Egypt (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 王之囚，埃及（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Pharaoh's butler and baker offend him and land in Joseph's block, each with a dream the same night. Joseph reads both: in three days Pharaoh will lift up the cupbearer's head and restore him, and hang the baker. Joseph begs the restored servant to 'remember me... and mention me unto Pharaoh' — and the butler forgets him for two full years.
summary.zh: 法老的酒政膳長得罪王，同囚於約瑟處，同夜各得一夢。約瑟解之：三日後法老必提酒政的頭復其職，而掛起膳長。約瑟求復職者「得的好處時候，求你記念我……在法老面前題說我」——酒政竟忘了他整整兩年。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Joseph said unto him: 'This is the interpretation of it: the three branches are three days; yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thine head, and restore thee unto thine estate; and thou shalt deliver Pharaoh's cup into his hand, after the former manner when thou wast his butler. But think on me when it shall be well with thee, and show kindness, I pray thee, unto me, and make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.'

The baker told his dream of birds eating baskets of baked foods from his head, and Joseph read death: 'within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh'. The third day was Pharaoh's birthday; the predictions came true exactly — 'and he gave the cup into the butler's hand; and he hanged the chief baker... yet did not the butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.' Paraphrase of Genesis 40:16-23 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Seven Kinds and Seven Ears: Pharaoh's Dreams
title.zh: 七母牛與七麥穗：法老之夢

region.en: Pharaoh's palace, Egypt (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 法老王宮，埃及（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Pharaoh dreams of seven fat kine eaten by seven lean and of seven good ears devoured by seven thin ones; his magicians fail. At last the butler remembers his fault, and Joseph, shaved and changed, stands before the throne: the doubled dream means the thing is certain — seven years of plenty, seven of famine. 'Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise' — and Pharaoh appoints him: 'there is none so discreet and wise as thou.'
summary.zh: 法老夢七肥牛被七瘦牛所吞，七好穗被七枯穗所食；術士皆不解。酒政終想起己過，約瑟剃面更衣立於御前：夢乃成雙，其事已定——七豐年七饑年。「法老當揀選一個有見識有智慧的人」——法老遂立之：「像這樣的人，有神的靈在他裡頭，我們豈找得著呢？」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying: 'It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.' ... Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt; and there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 41:16, 29-30 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

passages.text: Joseph advised storing a fifth of the harvest in the plenty years. Pharaoh told his servants no one had God's spirit like this man, and made him ruler of his house: 'only in the throne will I be greater than thou'. He set his signet on Joseph's hand, clothed him in fine linen, hung a gold chain on him, and rode the second chariot with the cry 'Bow the knee!' — naming him Zaphenath-paneah and giving him Asenath, daughter of Potipherah priest of On, as wife. Paraphrase of Genesis 41:34-45 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Spies from Canaan: The Brothers Before the Vizier
title.zh: 迦南來的間諜：眾兄在宰相前

region.en: Granaries of Egypt (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 埃及糧倉（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Famine drives ten brothers down for grain. The ruler they bow to, not recognizing, is Joseph; he remembers his dreams, speaks harshly as an 'interpreter of secrets', accuses them of spying, and tests them — Simeon bound, the rest sent home with grain and their money hidden in their sacks. 'And they said one to another: We are verily guilty concerning our brother', and Reuben's old reproach returns.
summary.zh: 饑荒驅十兄下埃及糴糧。他們所拜而不識的統治者正是約瑟；約瑟記起夢，以「解夢者」姿態嚴詞相待，指其為間諜，加以試煉——綁西緬，餘者糴糧返家，銀子皆藏袋中。「他們彼此說：我們在兄弟身上實在有罪」，流便舊責重提。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land. And Joseph's brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth. And Joseph saw his brethren, and he knew them, but made himself strange unto them, and spake roughly unto them.

He demanded they bring the youngest brother to prove their words, keeping Simeon bound 'before their eyes'; then commanded their sacks filled — and each man's money was returned secretly within it. At the inn one opened his sack and found the silver, 'and their heart failed them, and they were afraid, saying one to another: What is this that God hath done unto us?' Home, they told Jacob everything; he refused to let Benjamin go, crying: 'Me have ye bereaved... Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and ye will take Benjamin away.' Paraphrase of Genesis 42:9-38 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Judah's Pledge and the Feast at the Ruler's Table
title.zh: 猶大作保與宰相席上之宴

region.en: Granaries of Egypt (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 埃及糧倉（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Famine forces the issue. Judah pledges himself for Benjamin's safety and brings double money, balm, honey, and nuts. Joseph, seeing his full brother, orders a feast: the brothers are seated in birth-order, Benjamin's portions are five times the others', and Joseph asks after 'your father, the old man of whom ye spake, is he yet alive?' — and turns aside to weep.
summary.zh: 饑荒迫其決斷。猶大以身作保，攜雙倍銀、香料、蜜與榛子攜便雅憫往。約瑟見同母之弟，設宴款待：眾兄按長幼而坐，便雅憫所得五倍於人；約瑟問「你們所說你們父親那老人還在麼」——側身而泣。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And he asked them of their welfare, and said: 'Is your father well, the old man of whom ye spake? Is he yet alive?' And they answered: 'Thy servant our father is in good health, he is yet alive.' And he lifted up his eyes, and saw Benjamin his brother, his mother's son, and said: 'God be gracious unto thee, my son.' And Joseph made haste; for his bowels did yearn upon his brother; and he sought where to weep; and he entered into his chamber, and wept there.

title.en: The Silver Cup in the Sack of Benjamin

region.zh: 出埃及之路（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Joseph's steward hides the divining silver cup in Benjamin's grain-sack. Overtaken by pursuit, the brothers protest innocence — 'with whomsoever of thy servants it be found, let him die' — and it is found exactly in the youngest's sack. They rend their clothes and return together to the house, thrown down before the ruler.
summary.zh: 約瑟的管家將占卜銀盃藏於便雅憫袋中。追兵至，眾兄自稱清白——「在誰那裡搜出來，就叫他死」——而杯恰在幼弟袋中。他們撕裂衣服，同回宰相之屋，俯伏於地。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And he searched, and began at the eldest, and left at the youngest; and the cup was found in Benjamin's sack. Then they rent their clothes, and laded every man his ass, and returned to the city. Joseph's steward hides the divining silver cup in Benjamin's grain-sack.

title.en: Judah's Speech: I Will Be Surety for the Lad
title.zh: 猶大之言：我為這童子作保

region.en: Vizier's hall, Egypt (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 宰相之堂，埃及（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The longest speech in Genesis: Judah recounts the father who refused to part with the last son of his beloved wife, 'and now if thou take this also... it shall come to pass that when he seeth that the lad is not with us, he will die'. Judah offers himself as slave in the boy's place — and Joseph can no longer restrain himself.
summary.zh: 創世記最長演說：猶大述說那位不肯讓愛妻幼子離開的父親，「現在若把這個也帶去……他見沒有童子，就必死」。猶大以身代之為奴——約瑟再也抑制不住。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Thy servant my father said unto us: 'Ye know that my wife bare me two sons; and the one went out from me, and I said: Surely he is torn in pieces; and I saw him not since.' ... Now therefore when I come to thy servant my father, and the lad be not with us; seeing that his life is bound up in the lad's life; it shall come to pass, when he seeth that the lad is not with us, that he will die.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 44:27-31 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

passages.text: 'Let thy servant, I pray thee, abide instead of the lad a bondman to my lord; and let the lad go up with his brethren. For how shall I go up to my father, if the lad be not with me?' The man who had once proposed selling his brother now gave himself in exchange — and the test of the brothers was passed. Paraphrase of Genesis 44:33-34 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: I Am Joseph: The Revelation and the Descent Decreed
title.zh: 我是約瑟：相認與受命下埃及

region.en: Vizier's hall, Egypt (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 宰相之堂，埃及（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Joseph sends every Egyptian out and weeps aloud: 'I am Joseph; doth my father yet live?' His brothers are terrified to silence; he forgives in theological terms — 'be not grieved... for God did send me before you to preserve life'. Pharaoh hears of it and provides wagons; Jacob's spirit revives: 'Joseph my son is yet alive: I will go and see him before I die.'
summary.zh: 約瑟遣退埃及人，放聲大哭：「我是約瑟！我的父親還在麼？」眾兄驚惶失語；他以神學釋怨——「不要憂愁……這是神差我在你們前頭來，為要保全生命」。法老聞之賜車；雅各的靈甦醒：「約瑟還在，趁我未死以先，我要去見他一面。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Joseph said unto his brethren: 'I am Joseph; doth my father yet live?' And his brethren could not answer him; for they were troubled at his presence. And Joseph said unto his brethren: 'Come near to me, I pray you. And they came near. And he said: I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt. Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither; for God did send me before you to preserve life.'

title.en: The Descent into Egypt: Seventy Souls

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: At Beer-sheba Jacob offers sacrifices, and God speaks in visions of the night: 'fear not to go down into Egypt; for I will there make of thee a great nation... and Joseph shall put his hand upon thine eyes.' The family — seventy souls by the census — comes to Goshen; Joseph meets his father falling on his neck, 'and he wept on his neck a good while.'
summary.zh: 雅各在別是巴獻祭，神夜間異象中說：「不要害怕下埃及去，因為我必使你在那裡成為大國……約瑟必給你送終。」全家——按名數算七十人——至歌珊；約瑟迎見其父，伏在他頸項上「哭了許久」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And he said: 'I am God, the God of thy father; fear not to go down into Egypt; for I will there make of thee a great nation. I will go down with thee into Egypt; and I will also surely bring thee up again: and Joseph shall put his hand upon thine eyes.'

The genealogy of the seventy is recited by house. Judah was sent ahead to point out Goshen; Joseph harnessed his chariot and went up to meet Israel his father, and 'he presented himself unto him; and he fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while'. Israel said: 'Now let me die, since I have seen thy face, because thou art yet alive.' Paraphrase of Genesis 46:5-30 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Jacob Blesses Pharaoh and Settles in Goshen
title.zh: 雅各祝福法老，安居歌珊

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Five brothers present themselves and ask for the land of Goshen as shepherds' pasture; Pharaoh grants it. The aged Jacob is brought before the throne and blesses Pharaoh — 'and Pharaoh said unto Jacob: How old art thou?' — 'The days of the years of my pilgrimage are an hundred and thirty years... few and evil have the days of the years of my life been.'
summary.zh: 五兄自薦，求歌珊為牧羊之業；法老允之。老雅各被引至御前為法老祝福——「法老問雅各說：你平生的年日是多少呢？」——「我寄居在世的年日是一百三十歲……我平生的年日又少又苦。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Pharaoh said unto Jacob: 'How old art thou?' And Jacob said unto Pharaoh: 'The days of the years of my pilgrimage are an hundred and thirty years; few and evil have the days of the years of my life been, and have not attained unto the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage.' And Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from before Pharaoh.

title.en: The Younger Above the Elder: Ephraim and Manasseh
title.zh: 幼者居上：以法蓮與瑪拿西

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Near death, Jacob adopts Joseph's two Egyptian-born sons as his own. He crosses his hands — right hand on Ephraim the younger — and Joseph tries to correct him: 'Not so, my father'. But Israel answers, as if foreseeing the next generation's history: 'I know it, my son, I know it; he also shall become a people... but his younger brother shall be greater than he.'
summary.zh: 臨終之際，雅各收約瑟兩個埃及所生之子為己子。他交叉雙手——右手按幼者以法蓮——約瑟欲纠正：「不是這樣，我父。」以色列答，如預知下一代歷史：「我知道，我兒，我知道；他也必成為一族……只是他的兄弟將來比他還大。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. 'By thee shall Israel bless' made the Friday-night blessing of sons.

passages.text: And Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it upon Ephraim's head, who was the younger, and his left hand upon Manasseh's head, guiding his hands wittingly; for Manasseh was the firstborn. And when Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, it was evil in his eyes; and he held up his father's hand, to remove it from Ephraim's head unto Manasseh's head.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 48:14, 17 (public domain); verse 17 condensed.

passages.text: Joseph said, 'Not so, my father; for this is the firstborn'; but Israel refused: 'I know it, my son, I know it; he also shall become a people, and he also shall be great; howbeit his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations'. The blessing formula 'God make thee as Ephraim and as Manasseh' entered Jewish households permanently. Paraphrase of Genesis 48:18-20 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Israel gathers his sons: 'that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days'. Reuben is 'unstable as water'; Simeon and Levi are cursed for the sword at Shechem; Judah receives the royal oracle — 'the sceptre shall not depart from Judah... until Shiloh come' — while Zebulun, Issachar, Dan, Gad, Asher, Naphtali, Joseph, and Benjamin each get their tribe's character in poetry.
summary.zh: 以色列召集眾子：「把你們日後必遇的事告訴你們。」流便「如水滾沸」；西緬利未因示劍之刀受咒；猶大得王者諭言——「圭必不離猶大……直到細羅來到」——而西布倫、以薩迦、但、迦得、亞設、拿弗他利、約瑟、便雅憫各得支派之詩。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Judah's oracle underlies later messianic expectation; recorded as text.

passages.text: Judah, thee shall thy brethren praise; thy hand shall be on the neck of thine enemies; thy father's sons shall bow down before thee. ... The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the obedience of the peoples be.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 49:8, 10 (public domain); ellipsis marks omitted verse.

passages.text: Joseph's blessing is the longest: 'Joseph is a fruitful bough, a fruitful bough by a fountain; his branches run over the wall... from thence is the shepherd, the stone of Israel'. Benjamin is 'a wolf that raveneth'. Then, 'All these are the twelve tribes of Israel... and he charged them, and said unto them: Bury me with my fathers' — in the cave of Machpelah. Paraphrase of Genesis 49:22, 27, 28-29 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Funeral of Jacob and the Bones of Joseph

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Jacob dies and is embalmed after the manner of Egypt; a huge funeral procession of elders and chariots carries him to Machpelah, the Canaanites at the threshing-floor of Atad marvelling at 'a grievous mourning'. The brothers fear retribution; Joseph answers: 'ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good'. At a hundred and ten he dies, making his kin swear to carry his bones up — 'and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.'
summary.zh: 雅各死，照埃及例薰屍；長老與戰車大隊護送至麥比拉，亞達禾場迦南人驚歎「埃及人一場極大的哀哭」。眾兄懼報復；約瑟答：「從前你們的意思是要害我，但神的意思原是好的。」一百一十歲而卒，令親族起誓攜其骸骨上去——「收殮在棺材裡，停在埃及。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Joseph's bones motif returns in Exodus 13:19 and Joshua 24:32.

passages.text: And Joseph said unto his brethren: 'Fear not; for am I in the place of God? But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.'

Joseph and his father's household wept seven days at the threshing-floor of Atad beyond the Jordan. Then Joseph returned to Egypt, living to see Ephraim's children of the third generation; he told his brethren: 'God will surely remember you, and bring you out of this land... and ye shall carry up my bones from hence.' He died at a hundred and ten and was embalmed and coffined in Egypt — awaiting the exodus his oath presupposed. Paraphrase of Genesis 50:4-26 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
